_comment: Evergreen spotlights on govallecito.com's own site sections and story pages -- added 2026-07-26 as the 'site spotlight' leg of the grounded-content rotation (see generate_post_text.py's _try_build_grounded_content). Same discipline as seasonal_almanac.json: every headline/blurb below describes what's actually on the linked page, verified by reading that page directly this session -- nothing invented, no specific claims beyond what the page itself says. Unlike the almanac, these are NOT date-gated -- all always eligible, picked via deterministic day-of-year rotation. Left out of this first pass (not yet verified, add later the same way -- read the real page first): Respect Vallecito, First Visit, Living in Vallecito, Getting Here, Licenses & Permits, Launch Your Boat, and any individual named Featured Partner business (those are paid placements, not neutral informational content -- treated as a separate, not-yet-scoped decision, not bundled in here).

entries.headline: The week the creeks came up.
entries.blurb: govallecito.com's own account of the October 2025 flood — the hours as they happened, what was lost, and the eleven rescues.

entries.headline: 85 years of lake levels, charted.
entries.blurb: Every rise and fall since 1941 — the year the lake nearly filled, the year it nearly emptied, and why full pool now tops out at 96 percent.

entries.headline: The fire that changed how this valley thinks about fire.
entries.blurb: The Missionary Ridge Fire burned 73,000 acres and 56 homes in June 2002 — the Tour of Carvings' Alan Wyatt memorial honors a firefighter lost fighting it.

entries.headline: The gold camp that never paid.
entries.blurb: Tuckerville was a 1913 gold strike in Cave Basin that emptied out fast — a ghost-town story from above the lake.

entries.headline: A name on the map with real history behind it.
entries.blurb: Weaselskin Creek carries a documented Southern Ute name and history, kept honestly separate from the settler-era gold legend nearby.

entries.headline: The road above the east shore.
entries.blurb: Middle Mountain's forest road and ATV routes lead to a ghost town that technically isn't even in this county.
